estimatedFields: runway.lengthM and widthM (Wikipedia's 05R/23L, 15,024 x 300 ft, taken to be today's name of the 04/22 strip the orbiter used; the 1990 dimensions were not found) and runway.headingDeg (from the runway number)
touchdown.keas (the report gives 180 knots ground speed with a 4 kt headwind, not KEAS; ground speed used)

rollout.stopFt (the report gives the wheels-stop time, 62 s after the mains, not the distance: constant deceleration from 180 kt over 62 s, 9,418 ft, plus the 1,176 ft main-gear point; calibrated against STS-93's flown 6,777 ft, which this method overstates by about 5 percent)
rollout.brakeAfterMainFt (braking began at 119 kt at an average 6 ft/s2, 3,363 ft before the stop; the report gives no distance)
taem.mach, taem.altFt, taem.rangeNmi (the 2006 guidance workbook's nominal values; taem.met is the report's major mode change 305, which it labels terminal area energy management)

approach (the workbook's 20 deg and 1.5 deg glideslopes and preflare at 2,000 ft; gear down at 250 ft is the STS-1 press-kit plan value; the report gives only gear down and locked 13 s before the mains)
entry.reversalsMach (no per-flight list of the roll-reversal Mach numbers was sourced; left empty)

provenance.l: STS-31 Mission Report (NASA, 1990): deorbit burn 119:12:37:36.05 GMT, 291.0 s, 571.2 ft/s; entry interface 119:13:19:29.28; major mode change 305 at 119:13:43:36.25; main gear 119:13:49:56.25 at 180 kt ground speed, 1,176 ft past the threshold, 3 ft/s sink; nose gear 4,564 ft; braking at 119 kt, 6 ft/s2 average; wheels stop 119:13:50:58.25; concrete runway 22, Edwards; no blackout (TDRS). Launch 114:12:33:50.99 GMT
Entry, TAEM and Approach/Landing Guidance Workbook 21002 (2006): TAEM at about Mach 2.5, 60 n mi, 83 kft; 20 deg outer and 1.5 deg inner glideslopes, preflare about 2,000 ft
Wikipedia, Edwards Air Force Base: runway 05R/23L, 15,024 x 300 ft (4,579 x 91 m)
